ROUND 3 RESUBMISSION (2026-08-11), after the round-2 REVISE (gating objection from debug_historian). Everything below the marker is the round-2 rationale, unchanged. This preamble answers each objection with what is now FACT rather than plan: every edit shipped on commit c21af5eda, is live on chassis v1.0.1283 (pod-proven on BOTH replicas: 4 added literals present, a pre-existing positive control present, a fabricated negative control 0 — RUNBOOK R5 has the exact commands), and the backfill was applied post-roll (census 10 -> 1, the DO/RAISE guard printed its success notice). Review here is after the fact by design (owner ruling 2026-07-29: a thread cannot hold a change out of the fleet, so the gate reviews what shipped).

GATING — debug_historian, high: the backfill guard hardcodes 'exactly 1 unresolvable row remains' instead of deriving its expectation at run time. CONCEDED AS DISCIPLINE, and here is what actually happened: the guard fails CLOSED in both directions (10 remaining = script inert, 0 remaining = it repaired the row it was ordered to leave), so census drift between authoring and apply produces a spurious ABORT, never a wrong COMMIT. At apply it raised its success NOTICE at exactly 1, and the reader-predicate census independently re-verified 1 on 2026-08-11 (the fleet has since grown to 198 page+section rows; still exactly 1 invisible). The objection's principle is accepted for future files: a post-state count is the author's prediction, and the stronger form asserts row IDENTITY of the touched set against the file's own needle-gate selection (the RETURNING output already exists for exactly that). Recorded in the lane NOTES so the next migration author inherits the rule, not the luck.

At authoring time page_canonical.go carried another session's uncommitted FlatURLs work (since landed as 57a7fcbb4) and a pathspec commit cannot exclude a same-file passenger. === ROUND 2 RATIONALE, UNCHANGED, FOLLOWS ===

bugs_open/214. WriteSitePlanAction canonicalises page identity for two of the three tables it writes and not for the third, inside one function about sixty lines apart: site_plan_pages.name and site_plan_sections.page_name both come from datahelpers.CanonicalisePage, while site_plan_imagery.scope_ref is copied verbatim from the planner LLM's map key. CanonicalisePage deliberately collapses spellings onto one identity — the section-index family turns 'about' into 'about-index', 'contact' into 'contact-index', 'news' into 'news-index' — so the planner emits imagery.pages['about'], the plan writes its page as 'about-index', and the imagery row names a page ITS OWN PLAN DOES NOT CONTAIN. Nothing rejects it: buildImageryRow never inspects scopeRef. This is a platform defect, not an LLM one: the planner keyed the name it was given and the platform renamed the page underneath it. The consequence is not a broken image but a MISSING one — every consumer selects the plan row by scope_ref then joins the asset on assets.asset_key = spi.key, so an unmatched scope_ref yields an asset that was planned, generated, deployed, paid for and referenced by nothing, which is bugs_open/114's symptom reached through this cause. Measured live 2026-08-10 on current plans: 176 page+section-scope imagery rows, 10 invisible to every consumer, 8 of the 10 with an assets row already at status='active'. The fix resolves the page part of every imagery scope_ref through the plan's OWN raw-to-canonical map (built from planRows, which are already canonicalised and deduped at that point), keeps an unresolvable ref byte-identical to today plus a durable agent_error_log row, and adds the dedupe guard that the resolution itself makes necessary.

plan.summary: Resolve imagery scope_refs onto the page names the plan actually contains, at the only door that writes them; record what cannot be resolved; guard the unique index against the collapse the resolution makes possible.

edits.rationale: REVISED FROM ROUND 2 (which proposed exporting datahelpers.NormaliseSlug — withdrawn). planPageRow.RawName is normaliseSlug'd by ValidateRoles (page_role_validator.go:148), so the imagery map key must be normalised identically before lookup. The shipped route calls the EXPORTED CanonicalisePage with Role 'content': its default branch applies exactly that normalisation, and the homepage collapse runs first, so 'home' resolves to 'index' — the name the plan actually writes — which a bare NormaliseSlug would miss. The coupling to another function's internal branch is real and is therefore PINNED BY TEST (TestNormalisePageKey_MatchesTheNormalisationValidateRolesApplies asserts agreement with ValidateRoles across seven spellings AND asserts the deliberate 'home'->'index' divergence). No second implementation of slug normalisation exists in this change.

Maps every spelling the plan knows for a page onto the canonical name it actually holds. Built from planRows, which are already canonicalised AND deduped when imagery is flattened — so there is no second canonicalisation and none is possible anyway: CanonicalisePage requires a Role to choose between the tool-/guide-/game- prefix, the -index suffix and the homepage collapse, and an imagery ref carries no role. Pass 1 is identity (every canonical name maps to itself), which is what makes 'rows that work today are untouched' true by construction rather than by inspection. Pass 2 adds raw/slug aliases, and an alias two different pages would claim is REMOVED rather than resolved arbitrarily — a confident wrong rewrite is worse than none, and the ref then falls through to the miss path where it keeps today's behaviour and leaves a record. Follows buildPageFeatureMap (apply_adoption_plan_action.go:776-834), the same package's existing precedent for this exact class, upgraded with the durable log that one lacks. SHIPPED: write_site_plan_imagery_scope.go:147; Pass 2 (the alias arm round 2 objected was unshown) is at :158 and is quoted in the sketch verbatim.

The resolution itself. Section refs split on the FIRST colon — the split every consumer already performs (flag_page_image_rebuild_action.go:120, and the LIKE <page> || ':%' join in plan_sections) — and the remainder is reattached WITH its colon, so a reassembled ref keeps the colon chk_scope_ref_consistency demands of a section ref by construction rather than by a special case. An unresolvable ref is kept verbatim, which is byte-identical to pre-fix behaviour, so no row can regress. A guard refuses to write a colon into a page-scope ref because chk_scope_ref_consistency forbids it and a violation would abort the entire plan write.

The ordinal is VALIDATED AND RECORDED, NEVER REWRITTEN — a deliberate decision taken from the consumer census rather than from the bug file's pre-census candidate list. Three reasons. (1) No consumer parses the ordinal: the section join is LIKE-prefixed and keyed by asset key, and flag_page_image_rebuild splits it off and discards it, so an out-of-range ordinal on a correct page part is behaviourally inert today. (2) Rewriting risks 23505 on idx_site_plan_imagery_unique and breaks the (plan_id, scope, scope_ref, key) lock-transfer match for a further generation. (3) The correct value is unknowable at this seam: ordinal shift happens in ValidateSitePlanAction, a different action, and the pre-drop array is gone by the time write_site_plan runs. So the filing's flavours 1 and 3 become observable rather than repaired, which is the honest ceiling here; the structural fix is 214 candidate 2 (imagery inside the section entry, RFC_016 section 1) and is flagged as architecture-scope, not taken.

edits.rationale: idx_site_plan_imagery_unique is UNIQUE on (plan_id, scope, COALESCE(scope_ref,''), key). Canonicalisation is a COLLAPSING map, so a planner that keys one page under two spellings with a shared imagery key now produces two rows carrying one identity and the insert aborts THE WHOLE PLAN WRITE with 23505 — bugs_open/215 verbatim on the neighbouring table, where dedupePlanPageRows exists for exactly this reason. Measured: zero collisions on any current plan today, so this is NOT a live repair; it is here because the resolution above is what creates the possibility, and shipping the collapse without the guard would introduce the 215 failure mode to a second table. Merge rule: the entry whose ref was NOT rewritten wins, because the planner keying a page by the plan's own real name is the better-aimed of the two.

IMAGERY_SCOPE_REF_UNRESOLVED / IMAGERY_SCOPE_REF_ORDINAL_ANOMALY at severity warning, via LogActionError, following recordFactCarryMisses (v3_site_actions.go:3325-3359): accumulate typed misses during the pure pass, record them all in one function afterwards, so the resolution logic stays pure and unit-testable. Called AFTER tx.Commit(): agenterrors.Write takes *sql.DB and cannot join the tx anyway, and post-commit recording means a rolled-back plan write leaves no error rows describing imagery that was never persisted. The durable record is the whole point of the miss path — pod logs rotate under a second on the chassis and collected_data is pruned at ~24h, so without this row a scope_ref that matches nothing produces exactly the output a working one produces, for ever.

Three wiring changes. (i) Block 2c calls the resolution between flatten and the insert, using planRows as the authority. (ii) flattenImageryBlock now walks its page/section map keys in sorted order: Go randomises map iteration, and the dedupe guard resolves collisions by first appearance, so without this the survivor of a collision would differ between two runs over identical input and no test could pin it. (iii) transferImageryLocks gains a canonical fallback, because the fix creates a one-generation transition — the previous plan's locked row still says 'about:2' while the new row now says 'about-index:2', so the exact match affects zero rows and a human-approved lock is silently dropped. The fallback runs ONLY after the exact match has already found nothing, so it cannot alter any transfer that succeeds today, and it retires itself from the second post-change replan. SHIPPED at block 2c. sectionCountByPage — round 2 flagged it as a silently-missing helper — is a real shipped function (write_site_plan_imagery_scope.go:193: canonical page name -> section count, built from the same planRows).

Repairs only the 10 already-written rows; the code fix is what stops new ones. Touches a row only when it is BOTH unresolvable today (its page part matches no pages.name on that site — the vocabulary consumers actually join against) AND rescuable (its own plan holds a '<ref>-index' page that DOES resolve). A row that works today fails the first predicate and cannot be touched. A row with no canonical variant is deliberately left rather than repointed at a guess. The closing guard is a DO/RAISE, not a SELECT, because ON_ERROR_STOP does not fire on a non-empty result set and a verify block of SELECTs cannot stop a COMMIT; it aborts unless exactly 1 unresolvable row remains, which fails in BOTH directions — 10 means inert, 0 means it touched the row it was told to leave. EXECUTED 2026-08-10 post-roll: both UPDATEs ran with RETURNING (id, key, old->new ref); the guard raised its success NOTICE at exactly 1 remaining; a separate 373_bugfix_214_..._ROLLBACK.sql generated from the RETURNING output preserves every pre-change value. Independently re-verified 2026-08-11 at the reader's own predicate: 198 page+section rows fleet-wide, exactly 1 invisible to consumers (the deliberately-left tools-index). The guard's hardcoded expectation is conceded as the weaker pattern — it fails closed (abort, never wrong-commit), but future files should assert row IDENTITY of the touched set instead; recorded in lane NOTES.

plan.risks: WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY OPEN. (1) The rewrite arm is live but UNOBSERVED in production: no site holding -index pages has replanned since the roll (verified 2026-08-11 — the only post-roll plans are two pool sites with zero -index pages). Close condition stated in the rationale; deliberately not forced on a customer site. (2) mortgagecalculator's tools-index names a page existing under no spelling — a human decision, escalated in the lane handoff, protected by the backfill guard. (3) The 2-item ItemKey drift class (mortgagecalculator about/contact, both deferred) is now the imagery lane's documented call: re-key, cancel or leave on that site's next replan. (4) The one-generation lock-transfer fallback has no lock-pipeline-owned test to run against it — stated as a gap in the cross-lane notice, not claimed as covered. WHAT A REVIEWER SHOULD PROBE: the round-2 consumer-census caveat stands — a census cannot see a queue-built or external caller of scope_ref; and the stale-pages.name scenario (a DO NOTHING pages writer outliving a plan change) remains a visible-behaviour-change path that I believe is correct but have not observed live.
